verifications.claim: Artemis II is scheduled to splash down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California, on Friday, April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'precise splashdown in the Pacific Ocean, about 60 miles (100 kilometers) off the coast of San Diego'; R3: 'splash down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California, at approximately 8:07 p.m. ET on Friday, April 10, 2026'; R4: 'splashes down in the Pacific Ocean off the San Diego coast'; R5: 'splashed down off the coast of San Diego'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm the exact location and date.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is scheduled to splash down at approximately 8:07 p.m. ET (00:07 GMT on April 11).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'successful splashdown of NASA's Artemis 2 astronauts at 8:07 p.m. EDT'; '8:07:27 p.m. EDT (0007:27 GMT)'; R3: '8:07 p.m. ET'; R4: '00:07 GMT (8:07pm ET on April 10)'; R5: '8:07 p.m. ET'
verifications.reasoning: Exact time and timezone conversion match across sources.

verifications.claim: Artemis II follows a 10-day crewed lunar flyby.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '10 days after today's successful splashdown'; '10-day journey to the moon and back'; '10-day Artemis 2 mission'; R5: '10-day journey around the moon'
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe it as a 10-day mission; minor discrepancy with R2's '9 days' but primary live coverage supports 10-day.

verifications.claim: Recovery teams will retrieve the crew from the Orion spacecraft.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Recovery teams have reached the Orion spacecraft'; 'NASA and U.S. Navy recovery teams'; 'helicopters are now retrieving each of the four Artemis 2 crewmembers'; 'All four Artemis 2 astronauts have exited their Orion spacecraft'
verifications.reasoning: Detailed description of recovery process directly supports claim.

verifications.claim: Artemis II landing time is approximately 8:07 p.m. EDT (17:07 PDT).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '8:07 p.m. EDT'; timezone conversion matches 17:07 PDT (3-hour difference).
verifications.reasoning: Exact time in EDT confirmed; PDT equivalent correct.

verifications.claim: NASA+ and YouTube will provide live streaming starting around 6:30 p.m. ET.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA's live coverage ... will officially begin at 6:30 p.m. EDT'; R3: 'NASA's YouTube live stream of the event beginning at 6:30 p.m. ET'
verifications.reasoning: Direct confirmation of live streaming start time on NASA platforms including YouTube.

verifications.claim: Artemis III is planned to land astronauts on the Moon in mid-2027.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Artemis III (mid-2027) ... Crewed test of HLS in low Earth orbit'; no mention of lunar landing for III, landing planned for IV.
verifications.reasoning: Reference explicitly states Earth orbit tests for III, lunar landing for IV.

verifications.claim: Artemis IV is planned to land astronauts on the Moon in early 2028.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Artemis IV (early 2028) is planned to be the first American crewed lunar landing'
verifications.reasoning: Direct match on mission, timeline, and landing objective.

verifications.claim: The April 10 splashdown marks the safe return of the first crewed mission to the vicinity of the Moon in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first crewed mission to the vicinity of the Moon in over 50 years'; R2: 'first crewed flight beyond low Earth orbit since Apollo 17 in 1972'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm historical significance and date aligns with splashdown.
